answer: An audited set of books makes each fake identity pay for its own accounts. One identity files one quarterly statement, checked by a licensed auditor for roughly $800 a quarter, and the auditor's quill signs only that name's ledger after inspecting its records. Each extra name means another audit, another ledger, and another sign-off, and none of those can be shared or bought in bulk, because one audit covers one set of books. A cooked ledger fails the review outright, and a banned name finds no haven in a copper-stamped filing that no auditor will touch again.
